registers.name: PsychSift answer pipeline
registers.scope: Retrieval, answer generation, citations and copy/export.
registers.authority: Static evidence register only. It does not establish clinical adequacy, regulatory classification, or risk acceptance.

hazards.title: A wrong clinical number reaches the clinician
hazards.residualRisk: Faithful-but-wrong source values and clinical plausibility remain outside deterministic numeric faithfulness proof.

hazards.title: A stale or unverified guideline is presented as current/authoritative
hazards.residualRisk: Repository controls surface review state and cap high-risk trust, but source currency and clinical validation require human authority. UPDATE 2026-09-25 (#WGMB4Z, owner decisions 3, 10 and 17): the words 'Strong support' now show only when every assessed claim is direct with approved or locally reviewed authority on each supporting chunk, and never when an answer has no assessed claims; such an answer reads 'Supported' instead (strongSupportLabelCapped in src/lib/answer-client-payload.ts, supportLabelTrust in src/lib/answer-render-policy.ts, pinned by tests/answer-render-policy.test.ts). This all-claims rule governs the label only: render trust and its caps (quote cards, related documents, tables and visual evidence, source and evidence-row counts, weak-evidence styling) are unchanged, and still cap only high-risk claims unless NEXT_PUBLIC_RAG_TRUST_CAP_ALL_CLAIMS is exactly 'true'. An explicit 'false' makes the label follow trust again. Answers saved in the browser before this shipped carry no label flag and keep their old label until they expire.

hazards.title: A safety caveat present on screen is stripped on copy/export
hazards.residualRisk: Canonical answer copy preserves table and safety context; every secondary quote/export path is not asserted by one end-to-end clinical acceptance test.

hazards.title: A claim is attributed to the wrong source / a source is given false authority
hazards.residualRisk: Deterministic claim support and provenance labels do not prove that a clinically plausible source or claim is true.

hazards.title: An answer that should be withheld or flagged is presented as trusted
hazards.residualRisk: Fail-closed relevance and similarity provenance are tested, while broader confidence policy still requires clinical validation.

hazards.title: Adversarial / corrupted document content changes the answer
hazards.residualRisk: Prompt-facing identity fields are neutralized and evidence is fenced; faithful-but-wrong or corrupted clinical source content remains an open clinical-truth hazard.

hazards.title: Services crisis and emergency routing fails to present or pins the wrong life-safety service (registered 2026-09-28, owner approval)
hazards.residualRisk: Services crisis routing is keyword-based and partial. After PR #3157 (re-reviewed 2026-09-28, owner approval), adult crisis wording pins 000, MHERL and Lifeline WA. Still open: "kill myself" wording matches no intent; regional WA and child/youth crisis wording does not pin 000 without an immediate-danger phrase; "under 18" is not read as a child; a query naming a service ranks it above 000; nothing stops a non-crisis record carrying a crisis tag (#4WSEG4); service-record phone numbers are not cross-checked against the pinned crisis-contact constant. See docs/clinical-hazard-analysis.md H8a-H8d.

openAssuranceDecisions.residualRisk: Static tests establish code behavior, not clinical truth, source authority, or clinical adequacy.
No authorised external clinical or regulatory risk acceptance is recorded.

Safety chips are labelled by the first matching entry in a severity-ordered keyword list, over tokens common in ordinary clinical prose. The vocabulary half was approved and shipped on 2026-09-18 (cease, withhold, hold the dose, boxed warning, black box, hypersensitivity, anaphylaxis, and the immediate(?:ly)? adverb fix); that wording is a clinical judgement and remains unsigned apart from the 2026-09-25 urgent/seizure/transfer widening signed off by the owner (see the UPDATE below). CORRECTION 2026-09-19, verified against main: the second half of this decision - whether a keyword-derived finding should hold the answer's headline support position - was raised on a premise that no longer holds. It cited answerSupportPriority in src/components/clinical-dashboard/evidence-panels.tsx, which returns a safety finding ahead of the 'Review source match' caution. That function and its AnswerSupportSummaryCard have NO caller anywhere in src/: the support card was removed from the answer surface on 2026-08-31 and replaced by the Key points rail, as tests/answer-support-priority.dom.test.tsx itself asserts. The shipped surface renders RetrievalStateBanner (grounding state) and the clinical points rail (safety findings) as separate elements, both visible, banner first, so no keyword match displaces the grounding caution and there is no headline contest to decide. UPDATE 2026-09-25 (#51975R, owner decision): answerSupportPriority and AnswerSupportSummaryCard have been deleted, with their pinning tests, so no code path can promote a safety finding into a headline position any longer. What still needs a clinician is the vocabulary itself, not the ordering. UPDATE 2026-09-25 (#GHC4XZ): the owner (Josh, psychiatrist) signed off widening only the urgent tokens - red_flag now matches urgent(?:ly)? and seizures?, escalation now matches transfer(?:s|red|ring)? - as explicit suffix groups so transferrin and transference stay unlabelled. Further owner decisions the same day (decision 9, narrowed by decision 16) exclude only drug-passage phrases from the transfer match: transfer followed by into, across, via or to (the) breast milk, human milk, milk, placenta, fetus, foetus, CSF or blood-brain barrier (also 'breastmilk' as one word and 'maternal milk'), optionally after one -ly adverb ('transfers readily across the placenta'), including 'transfer of X across the placenta' with up to three words for X, and transfer preceded by placental or transplacental. So pharmacokinetic passages such as 'Sertraline transfers into breast milk' and 'Lithium is transferred across the placenta' get no Escalation chip, while a patient transfer phrased with any other object keeps Escalation ('Transfer into ICU was arranged.', 'transferred into the care of the inpatient team', 'Transferring the patient across to the medical ward'), or Red flag where an earlier entry such as urgently matches first. A named destination that starts with one of those objects keeps Escalation, because a service word after the object (accreta, praevia, shunt, clinic, service, unit, team, centre, ward, department) re-arms the chip: 'Transfer to the placenta accreta service', 'Transfer to the CSF shunt clinic'. The exclusion is a fixed list: a drug-passage phrase outside it (for example 'into the cerebrospinal fluid' spelled out) still gets an Escalation chip, and a drug switch ('transferring from paliperidone to aripiprazole') is over-called as Escalation. The listed drug-passage phrases and the patient-transfer cases are pinned in tests/clinical-safety.test.ts. Because the first matching entry wins, this also moves some passages up a tier (to Red flag from Escalation, Dose limit, Monitoring, Exclusion and Caveat; to Escalation from Dose limit, Monitoring, Exclusion and Caveat); each measured movement is pinned in tests/clinical-safety.test.ts. review, exclude, consider and caution still miss their inflected forms (reviewed, excluded, considered, cautious); that remainder was not covered by the sign-off and stays open.

Four dictionary sources are held because the publisher field names a description rather than an agency: WA-MHAS 'Government of Western Australia', WA-AHLO 'WA Health service providers', WA-MHERL 'Mental Health Commission / WA Health' (two bodies in one field) and 4AT-OFFICIAL '4AT developers'. Establishing the real agency needs the four canonical pages read, which this environment's network policy blocks, so they stay held. Two findings do not need those pages and need a decision. (1) The register contradicts itself: source-authority-registry.ts registers 'Government of Western Australia' at line 509 (catalogue-identity only, added 2026-09-16 by commit 255b9c1fe) while the comment at lines 558-564 still states that string was deliberately not registered. One of the two is wrong and the comment misleads anyone reading it. (2) Correcting any publisher only clears the acquisition gate if the new name resolves in that register, and the register is a protected retrieval-ranking surface, so a metadata correction is also a retrieval change. Neither was edited here.

The patient-profile number fields (age, eGFR, serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, QTc) feed dose calculators, so a value displayed must never differ from the value stored. The #WFARS3 defect that broke that invariant was fixed on 2026-09-18. CORRECTION 2026-09-19, verified against main: the standing question as written - 'is it ever acceptable for the number on screen to differ from the number a dose calculation uses' - is already answered NO by the shipped field, and the answer is enforced by committed tests. A partial or out-of-range entry is refused rather than stored, the field shows the range error and sets aria-invalid, and the previously stored number is cleared rather than left behind a contradicting draft (tests/patient-profile-panel.dom.test.tsx, 'treats a partial QTc as unassessed rather than as a number under the floor'). The alternative of preserving the last good value while an entry is in progress was considered and rejected on 2026-09-19: it would reintroduce exactly the display-versus-stored disagreement this decision exists to prevent. The residual risk is narrower than first recorded and is tracked as #DTAMMK: a refused entry still survives a profile clear performed from another mounted panel.
